Meanwhile, analysts and Semafor reporting suggest that despite both sides' dueling claims, a small fleet of oil tankers is actually running the waterway, forming a de facto new status quo. Hormuz traffic has fallen to near a 3-month low and US gas prices have hit a historic high for mid-August. UK Treasury officials warn UK growth could slow to just 0.3% in 2027 if Hormuz remains effectively closed through year-end. The conflict has spread to the Red Sea, where a Houthi attack killed 6 people — the first Red Sea fatalities in over a year — including 3 Pakistani nationals; the US has struck a containership in the area. Qatar says Oman-Iran negotiations over shipping are making major progress. Pakistan's defense minister had earlier said the US and Iran were close to some arrangement, while Pakistan's foreign minister condemned the Houthi attacks. Trump has publicly confirmed he was secretly moved away from Air Force One in a catering truck in Turkey at the Secret Service's direction to evade an assassination threat after the NATO summit. Oil had surged ~3% above $83/barrel, with further rises on Red Sea supply concerns. As the conflict drags on, Iran is also moving to deepen economic ties with BRICS nations: Iran's central bank chief announced Iran is set to join the BRICS New Development Bank. The war is also exacting a significant material cost on the US military: the Pentagon has lost at least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones — roughly 25% of its Reaper fleet — shot down or crashed in the conflict, at a total cost exceeding $1.3 billion, per Washington Post reporting citing three US officials.

Separately, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, 28 — the youngest-ever person to hold the role — has announced she will step down at the end of August to focus on her family, including her newborn second child, a daughter named Viviana born in May. Leavitt called it a "bittersweet decision" and effectively acknowledged that balancing the role with motherhood was harder than she had previously suggested publicly. Trump confirmed the departure and said she will continue as an outside adviser. CNN reported, citing anonymous sources, that Trump had repeatedly called Leavitt during her maternity leave demanding to know when she would return — a characterization that reframes Trump's previously reported "pleading messages" as more pressuring than supportive. Notably, the DOJ issued a memo extending executive privilege to "private advisers" just two days before Leavitt announced her outside adviser role, raising questions about the timing. Leavitt's departure stunned many insiders, and officials confirm Trump had no plan to replace her at the time of the announcement; top officials will cover briefings in the interim. Leavitt's departure statement posted on X carried a "Made with AI" tag, with the Daily Beast reporting she used AI to alter her image in the post. Her exit comes less than three months before the midterm elections, and Trump's approval rating has fallen to a record low per YouGov polling. Scott Jennings, a MAGA political commentator known for CNN appearances, has emerged as the frontrunner to replace her, with Kalshi odds now at 29% after a 24-point spike in 24 hours, though Jennings himself has dodged when asked about the role. Alina Habba, Stephen Miller, and Trump personal aide Natalie Harp (at 5% Kalshi odds) have also been floated as candidates.

The WHO warns the outbreak — caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments — is on track to become the deadliest Ebola outbreak in history. The UN Secretary-General says cases are doubling every 20 days, threatening to eclipse the 2014-2016 West African epidemic. WHO has revealed the outbreak spread undetected for months, suggesting its true scale is far larger than official counts. Over 2,000 people have been killed.

In a new domestic dispute, the Trump-appointed Kennedy Center board has voted to partially close the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts for up to two years for a $250 million renovation, and to inscribe Trump's name on the facade — defying a federal judge who had previously ordered Trump's name removed and temporarily blocked a similar closure roughly three months ago. A former Israeli prime minister has called the broader settler campaign a "concerted and meticulous attempt at ethnic cleansing" against Palestinians. Separately, Israel simultaneously inaugurated a new emblematic settlement elsewhere in the West Bank.
